> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fix DNS tests fail with IPv6 https://testgrid.k8s.io/conformance-kind#kind%20(IPv6),%20master%20(dev)

The tests were failing because were trying to use a global variable that's only populated in one of the test executors when running in parallel.

It also make the DNS tests single IP family, because using a probe command asking for A and AAAA records in the command line can lead to false positive, since the command is doing a logical OR instead of a logical AND, that will needed in dual stack clusters.

```
func (tc TestContextType) ClusterIsIPv6() bool {
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/45d6f08868ce2729182aae5734a00e5e27ae08f9

Sorry if I'm missing context. 

`IPFamily` shouldn't change across parallel ginkgo nodes so curious why we moved the default IP family check into `SetupSuiteAllNodes`.

> Previously ,TestContext.IPFamily was set on framework.SetupSuite(), but it turns out that part of the code only runs on just one parallel node in the first function of SynchronizedBeforeSuite(), thus the variable wasn't available for the rest of the nodes.

So `TestContext.IPFamily` is set _by_ the first parallel node, but does that mean it's not readable from other parallel nodes after the fact? `TestContext` a global var so I assumed it is.

> So `TestContext.IPFamily` is set _by_ the first parallel node, but does that mean it's not readable from other parallel nodes after the fact? `TestContext` a global var so I assumed it is.

right, actually I was thinking the same when I've implemented it but seems that `TestContext` is global per node executor, not global for all the nodes.

So is it that `TestContext` is not updated for all other node executors or that because they run in Parallel there are race conditions where we check for IPFamily before it's set by the first node? 

Wondering if we should move this to `AfterReadingAllFlags` in `test_context.go`, no need to this run per node if it doesn't change across suites.

The first node cannot modify `TestContext` in other nodes because each node runs in a separate process.

`AfterReadingAllFlags` is called by all processes, processing the same input, and thus the result is the same on all nodes. The `getDefaultClusterIPFamily(c)` call could work there, but I think it's better to call it where it is called now because of the need to connect to the API server. Doing that in `AfterReadingAllFlags` "feels" a bit too early.

I've tried that approach but with the capital `-I` you obtain *all* the IP addresses, and it overcomplicates the bash oneliner.
```
root@kind-control-plane:/# hostname -i
172.17.0.4
root@kind-control-plane:/# hostname -I
10.244.0.1 10.244.0.1 172.17.0.4 fd00::1 fd00::1 2001:db8:1::242:ac11:4
```
The `getent` command was used previously and worked fine, I tried different things to try to consolidate that line but didn't find a better option, I'm really open to suggestions
